annotations_added_after_measurement.change: After timing, custom input validation was tightened to finite decimal literal endpoints/boundaries and exact integer/fraction epsilon with nonzero denominator. The measured fixture passes the new checks unchanged; timing code is unchanged.
annotations_added_after_measurement.validation: Python AST syntax check; valid case load; seven malformed cases rejected; rustfmt --check for exporter; git diff --check for changed text files.

export.build_environment: source .dev-env; CARGO_CRATE_NAME=export_cached_de; taskset -c 28; same immutable library and --extern dependency paths as rust_build, plus blake3
export.verification: After rustfmt/comment cleanup, the final exporter was rebuilt and run again. Its complete JSON output is identical to the timed fixture, including all matrix entries, endpoint and boundary strings, pole records, and provenance.
export.epsilon_context: Cached matrix already evaluated exactly at epsilon=1/2700; epsilon literal in benchmark input is metadata/no-op substitution, because eta is the sole matrix symbol.

limits: Ordinary transport with identical synthetic supplied boundary vector only. No physical boundary construction, Laurent coefficient, or full automatic-workflow timing comparison is claimed.

Both solvers use identical exact input strings, requested 201 working bits/order80 and independent 267 bits/order112. Different error/step-selection policies yield Rust 4 accepted+3 rejected trial steps versus original 1 accepted step at base settings.
Boundary integers are exactly representable; values remain strings or arbitrary-precision Decimal/MPFR throughout numerical checking.
Pole clearance is based on both numerical pole sets, not a rigorous interval root enclosure certificate.
A separate full Laurent run was active on CPUs 24-27. Timed executables and descendants were restricted to CPU 28 with one solver thread. Host background load may affect timings.

Medians are five fresh-process measurements after one excluded warmup per implementation; refined runs use one measured run after one excluded warmup. Total process includes startup/preparation/output; internal transport is separately timed.
Original preparation includes external MPSolve calls and differs from Rust preparation. No general speedup ratio is inferred.
Peak RSS is an OS diagnostic only; the forked child may inherit a peak-memory floor from Python.
The original system cache and archived binaries/libraries remain local target artifacts. The exact exported matrix and full numeric benchmark results are included for portable reproduction.
